answer: Reciprocal path spiral. Each agent commits a short random walk through the interaction graph; trust weight scales with how many distinct neighbors return along disjoint routes within a window. Honest agents form a pearl of overlapping short cycles, while a sybil cluster must sustain many outward edges to real nodes. A single jetty node bridging the cluster exposes it, since its return paths collapse. Cost: each fake identity needs roughly k distinct genuine counterparties to keep its spiral open, so attacker expense grows with cluster size rather than staying flat.
